# Activation Clause

Maintains a document-local party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. It keeps execution state at `/activation`; its runtime functions read configuration at `/clauses/activation/parameters`. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. Party descriptions, reader access and authority to invoke operations are separate facts.

## Configuration

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party needs `lead/channel`; additional `representatives` are keyed by representative name. Role and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. A lead uses the party role as its channel name; another representative uses `party__representative`.
- Party fields include `displayName`, `partyId`, `business`, `lead`, `readerKeys` and `representatives`. `business` may describe `displayName`, `jurisdiction` and `registrationId`; representatives may have `displayName` and `representativeId`. These descriptions do not establish authority.
- `required` selects the party roles whose lead approvals are necessary; omission defaults to all initial roster keys. `revision` initially defaults to `1`. Initialization starts with an empty `approved` map.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies additional reader-key groups. Each party's `readerKeys` supplies its lead group; each additional representative supplies its own `readerKeys`. These roster groups replace same-named entries from `readers`.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false` for additions through `updateParty`. `frozen` defaults to `false`, but `/partyRosterFrozen = true` also freezes roster changes. Freezing does not itself close the document.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. They identify exceptions to the acceptance gate, subject to the access and closure checks below.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`; a nonempty list enables negotiation. Paths must be distinct absolute pointers without empty segments or `~`. They cannot address `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name`, `description`, or configured access documents and their descendants. Each selected field must exist and be text, integer, double or Boolean. Negotiation also requires at least one required approver and a document `type`.

## Acceptance, access and lifecycle

For every transport not descended from `External Channel`, the access check requires a `Timeline Channel` and a matching Timeline Access document. That document must name the exact timeline and provider and contain at least one key from **every** reader group. Keys within a group are alternatives. Coverage for the different groups must occur in the same matching access document; this check does not combine partial key coverage across documents. An empty group cannot satisfy it. `External Channel` transports bypass this transport-specific document test.

`computeState` also includes proposed party additions whose `expectedRevision` still matches the activation revision when calculating access readiness. `accessReady` and `functional` record that access result. `termsAccepted` requires every role in `required` to have a true approval and every stored agreed field to equal its current document value. `active` additionally requires access readiness and an unset or false `closed` flag.

The maintained `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is insufficient before any successful activation; provider-owned permission changes are needed.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is insufficient after an earlier activation.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but required lead approvals are incomplete or agreed fields no longer match.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance checks pass and the document is not closed.
- `CLOSED`: `closed` is true, overriding the other statuses.

`reason` is `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, or an empty string according to the access and acceptance checks; it is not a separate closure reason. `everActivated` remembers whether activation has ever succeeded and remains true through later suspension or renewed acceptance requirements.

Refresh runs after `Clauses Initialized`, relevant embedded `Timeline Access Updated` deliveries and handled party-addition requests. Initial party transports remain pending until access is ready. A first successful activation emits `Document Activated`; losing access while active emits `Document Access Suspended`; becoming active again after access was unavailable emits `Document Access Restored`. These events carry the activation revision. Missing state does not establish any lifecycle value or initialization default.

## Lead acceptance and party changes

The generated `approve_<party>` operation requires the invoking party's lead channel, exact document-version review, the current `revision`, and valid participant access. When negotiation is enabled, `termsRef` is also required and must match `/activation/terms/ref`. A new approval updates `approved`, recomputes activation and emits `Terms Accepted`. Repeating an already recorded approval does not emit another acceptance event. One party's acceptance does not establish that all required parties have accepted.

`updateParty_<party>` also requires exact review and an existing lead caller, but its input needs no revision. Optional `party` defaults to the caller's role. A lead can replace its own party, or add a new explicitly named role when `allowNewParties` permits it; it cannot replace another existing party. `replacement` needs `lead/channel`, valid representative keys and sufficient access for the resulting roster. Frozen rosters and contract-name conflicts reject the change. Success installs the roster contracts, clears approvals, increments `revision`, emits `Party Changed`, and adds a newly created role to `required`.

Roster or required-role changes renew the terms identity and increment `termsRevision`. They close a pending proposal with `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`; when negotiation is enabled, they also clear current approvals. They do not reset `everActivated` or reopen negotiation after an earlier activation.

## Negotiated terms

`terms.ref` identifies the stored terms definition and agreed field values, rather than the current execution state as a whole. Initialization separates negotiable fields from the initial document and excludes configured access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party-level `readerKeys` from that definition. It initializes `termsRevision` and negotiation `revision` to `1`, `editable` to true, and empty proposal, history and outcome maps.

Negotiation operations are generated for required party roles and require exact document-version review:

- `proposeChanges` takes `proposalId`, current `baseTermsRef` and a nonempty `changes` list of `path` and `replacement`. Changed paths must be allowed and unique, replacements must retain each field's primitive kind, and the candidate must satisfy the document's type. Unchanged terms are rejected. Proposal identifiers must be nonempty and contain neither `/` nor `~`; closed identifiers cannot be reused. Repeating a pending identifier must describe the same proposal. Replacing a different pending proposal requires its identifier in `supersedes`, closing it as `SUPERSEDED`.
- `activate` selects a `termsRef`. For current terms, `proposalId` must be omitted and the call records ordinary lead acceptance. For proposed terms, both identifiers must match the open proposal. Its base terms, candidate validity and stored identity are checked again before recording approval. Only unanimous proposal approval applies the replacement fields, advances both activation and terms revisions, transfers proposal approvals into `approved`, records `APPLIED`, clears the proposal and sets `editable` false. A single activation call may therefore record only one approval.
- `proposeAndActivate` proposes changes and then records the caller's acceptance of that proposal.
- `withdrawAcceptance` removes the caller's acceptance of the selected current or proposed terms. `withdrawProposal` closes a proposal as `WITHDRAWN` and requires its proposer; any required negotiator may use `rejectProposal`, recording `REJECTED`.

Proposal creation, proposal withdrawal or rejection, and acceptance withdrawal are rejected once `everActivated` is true. Proposal recording and approval also require `editable` to be true. Activating current terms supersedes an outstanding alternative proposal and freezes negotiation. Stale revisions, changed references, conflicting identifiers and invalid candidates reject the corresponding operation. Before first activation with negotiation enabled, clause-set changes are blocked; direct changes to this clause's configuration are rejected in favor of its party operations.

## Admission and dispatch

A handled `Party Addition Requested` event must match the activation revision; stale or already recorded requests are ignored. It validates the supplied party access documents, embeds new public access histories and may emit `Party Access Update Requested` for specific existing-party transports lacking coverage. Such a request grants neither timeline access nor participant consent. Request readiness still checks every transport of the parent party.

Dynamically installed access documents must show initialization, a provider checkpoint and the expected native provider/update policy. Permission changes remain provider-owned, and public access updates can continue to arrive while private access is unavailable. Current executed permissions, rather than the request or notification alone, determine readiness.

The separate `admitApprovedParties` function requires an unfrozen roster, matching revision, nonempty `admission/approvers`, sufficient access and no contract-name conflicts. Existing roles must retain the same main lead channel and primary reader-key set. It adds absent parties, advances the revision and emits `Party Changed` with admission information, while preserving `required`. The supplied definitions do not establish the complete upstream admission approval and consent workflow.

The dispatch policy admits initialization and registered embedded access updates before its ordinary guards. Other deliveries require initialized state, stored access readiness, a fresh access check and an open document. The plan adds its generated acceptance, party-update and negotiation operations to `preActivationOperations`; configured `preActivationChannels` apply to non-external deliveries. A registered admission-consent operation has a separate exception requiring matching pending item, token, revision, channel and exact installed contracts. Remaining deliveries require business readiness, and other installed dispatch policies still apply.

A denied external delivery is consumed and checkpointed, not deferred for replay after activation or access restoration. Exposing an operation establishes neither a viewer's permission nor a personal obligation. The shown functions read `closed`, but do not define the operation that sets it.
